passage: The registration link closed at nine the next morning, and the power had gone out, so the family sat around one lamp in the shop's back room. Jasleen had a pencil and the back of a bill. “Two evenings before camp I'll work the counter till closing,” she said. Her mother tapped the wall calendar. “And during?” “Cousin Thomas can come. He said he's free that fortnight.” Papa raised an eyebrow. “Accounts?” “I'll fill the daily sheet on my phone every night from camp. Ten minutes.” Papa counted on his fingers: two evenings, a cousin, a nightly sheet. “Neither of us gets everything we wanted,” he said. “But nobody loses everything.” Jasleen hugged her mother, then rang Thomas by torchlight.

qa.q: How will Jasleen handle the accounts during camp?
qa.a: She will fill the daily sheet on her phone every night, about ten minutes.

qa.q: What might Jasleen have felt when Papa said nobody loses everything?
qa.a: Relief and gratitude: she hugged her mother and rang her cousin at once.

qa.q: What could the family try if Thomas could not come, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a neighbour's teenager or shorten the shifts, because the aim is to keep the counter covered without dropping the camp.

qa.q: How does the deal look to Thomas?
qa.a: Thomas is being asked to give up a fortnight of free time, so he would want proper notice and clear hours; his ready yes suggests he wants to help.

grounding: A family agrees two evenings of work, a cousin's cover and online accounts so both needs are partly met.

In their Andheri flat, Reena's family sat around the dining table with a calendar spread out between the plates. The robotics camp in Bengaluru was from the 10th to the 20th. The stationery shop's back-to-school rush ran through the whole month.

"Here's what I can do," Reena said, pen ready. "Before the camp, I'll work Thursday and Friday evenings at the counter."

Her father nodded slowly. "And during the camp?"

"Pradeep said he can help." Her cousin, home from college, raised a hand from the sofa. "Mornings only, but that's the rush."

"And the accounts?" her mother asked. "You always do the entries."

"I'll do them online every night from the hostel. Send you the sheet by ten."

Her father wrote it on the calendar in red. It wasn't everything anyone wanted. But everybody had something, and everybody had agreed to it out loud.

qa.a: From the 10th to the 20th, in Bengaluru.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt as her father wrote the plan in red?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and hopeful, since her camp was protected while the shop was still covered.

qa.q: What else could the family add to make the plan fairer?
qa.a: They could agree to check in halfway through the camp, so any gap at the shop is noticed and fixed quickly.

qa.q: How does the compromise look to Pradeep?
qa.a: Pradeep seems willing and helpful, raising a hand to take the morning rush while home from college.

grounding: Shows a family agreeing that the student works evenings before the camp, a cousin helps during it and she does the accounts online, so both needs are partly met.

"So if I go to the camp, who handles the flower orders for the Navratri weddings?" Bhavna's mother asked.

"Kamal bhaiya," Bhavna said. "I called him. He'll come from Nashik for four days."

Her elder cousin Kamal, on speakerphone, said, "Only four, though. After that I have exams."

"The camp's six days," her father pointed out.

"I know. So before I go, I'll work Monday and Tuesday evenings, and I'll make all the garlands for the first two weddings in advance. And every night from the camp I'll update the orders sheet on the phone."

Her mother crossed her arms. "And the last two days?"

"Can Masi help? She offered at Diwali."

Her mother thought. "She did."

Her father smiled for the first time that evening. "It's not perfect. But it might work."

qa.q: How many days can Kamal come from Nashik?
What does her father's first smile of the evening suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt relieved and reassured, seeing that Bhavna had thought through how the shop would manage.

qa.q: What could the family do if Masi can't help after all?
qa.a: They could reduce the number of orders taken for those two days, so no one is overwhelmed while Bhavna is away.

qa.q: How might Bhavna's mother see the plan?
qa.a: Her mother seemed sceptical at first, arms crossed, but she softened on remembering Masi's offer, which suggests growing trust in the plan.

grounding: Shows a family agreeing that the student works evenings before a camp, a cousin covers part of it and she updates orders online, so both needs are partly met.
